answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, transferable stake before it votes on a trade or earns rewards, then slash that stake when an independently verifiable fraud proof shows coordinated abuse. One operator can still create many accounts, but each must tie up capital, and a successful attack risks losing it; splitting identities no longer makes influence free. A juniper market might set the lock from observed risk, while karst describes its settlement layer and nadir the minimum stake.
